nodes.label: Knowledge ingestion idempotency is keyed on source identity, source version, content hash and pipeline version together (spec §29): reprocessing the same event never creates a second copy of the same knowledge, while a change in any one of the four is a legitimately new derivation rather than a duplicate — which is what makes re-parsing after a parser or embedding-model upgrade safe to run over the whole corpus. This is the ingestion-time rule; FR-081's `sha256(tenantId, connectionId, entityType, externalId, payloadHash)` re-delivery identity remains the raw-boundary rule beneath it, and BR-009's single-envelope discipline still governs how any surface reaches the pipeline at all.

Silent loss is the one outcome forbidden: a corpus that quietly omits what it could not parse reports a completeness it does not have, and every downstream answer inherits that overstatement without a way to detect it.

nodes.label: Per-Business domain visibility: `resolveViewer()` resolves which domains a principal may see **per Business**, not once per principal. Each Membership's grant applies only to the Businesses that Membership covers — an OWNER Membership confers all domains on the Businesses it owns, and never widens what the same principal sees in a Business where they hold only a MEMBER Membership. The route guard and the domain bar both read the per-Business answer.

nodes.label: Import target authorization: the FR-012 pipeline authorizes the Workspace it is about to write to, instead of accepting whichever `workspaceId` the request body names. All three intake routes (`/api/import/dry-run`, `/api/import/commit`, `/api/import/xlsx`) resolve a viewer, and the target Workspace is resolved **before** validation so an unauthorized target is refused without the caller learning anything about the plan. (a) A **Business-scoped** Workspace requires `ownsBusiness(viewer, workspace.businessId)` — the same predicate the other write paths use, not a second reading of it; a caller who may see the Business but does not own it is refused. (b) A Workspace **above Business** (`scopeType` PORTFOLIO or TENANT) is refused with an explicit reason stating that no authority above Business is declared — this requirement deliberately does **not** invent one. Enabling such an import requires a prior FR that makes portfolio/tenant authority *holdable*: a viewer-contract change in the manner of FR-061, since today no principal can hold it. The dry run is authorized identically to the commit — a read-only preview of another scope's contents is the leak the commit guard would otherwise still allow.

nodes.label: Repository ownership: a `Repository` is owned by exactly one Business (`Repository.businessId`), which is the decision FR-072 recorded as missing for `/api/repositories` and `/api/repositories/[id]`. Business rather than Tenant or Portfolio is forced, not chosen: the viewer contract carries only Business-keyed grants, so no principal can hold authority above Business (SDD-037) and a higher-scoped Repository would be ungovernable. nodes.label: Scope-creation authorization: every creator behind `POST /api/scope` resolves a viewer and is authorized at the scope it actually writes, in three tiers. Self-service is never unauthenticated: the viewer is resolved, the write is attributed, and an audit event is recorded.

nodes.label: Raw external ingestion boundary: every acquisition channel (webhook, pull, file, manual) converges on one normalized ingestion envelope carrying tenant, Business, connection, provider, lane, entity type, external id, source type and schema version, and a channel is added as an adapter rather than a second raw-write path. (a) Ingestion identity is `sha256(tenantId, connectionId, entityType, externalId, payloadHash)` over a canonically serialized payload, so a re-delivered event resolves to `UNCHANGED` instead of a duplicate row; the external id contributes to that identity and is never itself a key (BR-002). (c) Raw ingestion persists the source payload verbatim and never writes domain truth: translation into business entities is a separate later path, so a failed translation cannot corrupt the evidence it was derived from. (d) A run records its own counts and terminal state, and a failure is preserved as a DeadLetterRecord naming the failing stage and owner rather than being retried silently. This requirement declares the ingestion substrate only; no scheduler, no translation ACL and no reader surface is in scope.

Work stays assigned to a Person (`WorkItem.assigneeRef`), never to a Team (ADR-037 D4). FR-036's existing "project Team" tab is untouched and its reconciliation with this entity is deferred deliberately (ADR-037 D5).

nodes.label: Schema declaration for the live production-auth tables: `PersonCredential`, `PasswordResetToken` and `Workstream.laneId` exist on the Supabase database — `PersonCredential` with a real credential row and `laneId` with a distinct value on every Workstream — but existed in no committed schema, having been pushed there from the unmerged branch `codex/postgres-primary-runtime`. This requirement declares their shape so the schema describes the database that exists. It is deliberately **declaration only**: no service, route or UI is in scope, and the feature code remains on that branch. The reason it cannot wait for that branch to merge is that `prisma migrate diff` proposes `DROP TABLE "PersonCredential"` against an undeclared table, so any routine `db push` destroys a live credential without the operator reading the SQL. Registering the tables here removes the destructive suggestion without deciding the feature's fate. **Resolution (2026-08-26):** the branch was never merged and no longer needs to be — `main` grew its own superior implementations of everything it held (`PersonCredential` login/logout via FR-046/FR-095; password reset via FR-104, reimplemented rather than revived because the draft returned the raw reset token to the unauthenticated caller). Its FR-082/FR-083 claims stay burnt on the pipeline canvas. The branch is deleted; `Workstream.laneId` remains declared-only.

nodes.label: CRM Conversation Inbox — the reader surface for the LINE ingress. `Customer`, `Conversation` and `Message` have been written by the FR-023 ingest seam since the first LINE turn, and FR-081 declared in as many words that **no reader surface was in scope** — so every message this product has ever received is invisible to the operator whose business received it. This requirement adds that surface and nothing else. `GET /api/crm/conversations` returns one authorized, read-only list (customer, channel, message count, last-message preview and time, owning-Business label); `GET /api/crm/conversations/{id}` returns one thread with its messages oldest-first and the customer behind it. Scope follows **BR-001, not the shell**: the CRM is tenant-shared, so the list is the Tenant of the selected Business, restricted to conversations whose `businessId` is null (tenant-shared — which is what an unbound LINE binding writes, and therefore the common case) or a Business this viewer can already see. A viewer is never handed a conversation belonging to a Business they could not open. The `customer` domain slot leaves `soon` and gains `/customer` (Dashboard) and `/customer/conversations` (Inbox). It **writes nothing**: no reply box, no status transition, no read-receipt. Replying is BR-011 territory and belongs to the edge runtime that owns the reply — a console that could also reply would make two reply owners, which is the one thing BR-011 exists to prevent. `Conversation.status` is displayed as stored and no enum is declared for it, because nothing in this slice writes it.

nodes.label: LINE reply delivery receipt: the outbound half of a conversation becomes a row. Nothing has ever written a `Message` with `direction: 'OUTBOUND'` — the reply is assembled here, handed to the edge runtime, sent to the customer and then forgotten — so FR-091's inbox shows one side of every conversation and its `OUTBOUND` count is structurally zero. `POST /api/agent/line-delivery` accepts a batch of receipts from the transport owner, each naming the **inbound `Message.id` it answers** and the text that was **actually sent**. (a) The receipt comes from the edge runtime *after* a successful send and not from this side at hand-over, because the two differ: when the stack cannot answer, the transport sends its own fallback text, and recording what this side produced would record a message the customer never received (BR-011 — the reply owner is the one who knows). (b) Scope is resolved by the same seam as the webhook (FR-052), and the named inbound message must resolve inside that scope — a binding for one tenant can never attach a reply to another tenant's conversation (SEC-001). (c) Idempotent on `reply:<inboundMessageId>` as the message's external id, so a redelivered receipt resolves to the existing row: one inbound message has one reply, which is exactly what the LINE Reply API allows per token. (d) The row records the text the customer received; whether it came from the stack or from the transport's fallback is recorded on the audit event, not in the body, because the body is what was said and the provenance is a different fact. The webhook response gains `conversationId` and `inboundMessageId` so the transport has something to name — on the **failure** result as well as the success one, because a failed turn is precisely when the transport substitutes its own text and a customer certainly received something. That failure result also gains the `eventId` it never carried: the transport matches results to events by that field, so a failed result was previously unfindable and its fallback was sent only because an unmatched result and a failed one both read as "not ok". All additive; the four fields the transport already reads are untouched.

nodes.label: Owner-assisted password reset: a Business owner over a Business the target Person belongs to — the same authority boundary as FR-038 Membership administration — or the installation operator mints a single-use, one-hour, hash-bound reset token (`POST /api/platform/users/password-resets`), and the public `POST /api/auth/reset-password` consumes it: new `PersonCredential`, token burnt, **every active Session revoked**. The raw token appears exactly once, in the authenticated mint response, for out-of-band handover (LINE, in person); it is stored only as a SHA-256 digest and never logged or audited in any form. There is deliberately no public forgot-password route: with no mail transport, such a route either returns the token to the unauthenticated caller — an account-takeover primitive, which is what the abandoned FR-082 draft on `codex/postgres-primary-runtime` shipped and the reason it was not revived as-is — or returns nothing and resets nothing. Uses the `PasswordResetToken` table FR-090 declared (its `token` column now carries the digest).

nodes.label: Structural knowledge chunking with parent-child lineage: a parsed document is split along its own structure — document → section → chunk — rather than at a fixed token stride, and every chunk carries the eight fields FR-109's `DPS-KI-CHUNK` catalog row already fixes (`chunk_id`, `parent_id`, `document_id`, `sequence`, `heading_path`, `token_count`, `scope`, `provenance`). `heading_path` carries the whole ancestor chain rather than the nearest heading, so a chunk retrieved on its own still says where in the document it came from. A section too large to retrieve as one unit additionally gets overlapping fixed windows beneath it, parented to the section chunk and reported as a warning — the fallback the specification names (§12), never the default; the windows overlap because without it a sentence lying across a boundary is left whole in neither. Chunking derives nothing it is given: `scope` comes from FR-111 classification and `provenance` from Stage 3, both upstream. The function is pure — no I/O, no clock, no randomness — so the same document chunks to the same ids every time, which is what lets BR-021 treat a reprocessed document as the same knowledge rather than a duplicate. Stage 7 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.

nodes.label: Entity candidate extraction from chunks and structured records: FR-112's chunks and caller-named record fields both yield `EntityCandidate` objects carrying the six fields FR-109's `DPS-KI-ENTITY-EXTRACT` catalog row fixes — `candidate_id`, type, mention, `normalized_name`, `source_chunk_id`, `confidence` — plus the originating chunk or record, the scope it was found in, and the provenance carried from that source so the chain back to the raw artifact survives, so a candidate can never be read outside its tenant (SEC-001, BR-001). Recognition is a seam with a deliberately narrow deterministic default (SDD-060); a record mention is read from a declared field rather than guessed, and carries confidence 1 for that reason. Pure — no I/O, no clock, no randomness, no model — so the same input yields the same candidate ids, which is what lets BR-021 treat a reprocessed document as the same knowledge. Stage 8 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.

nodes.label: Canonical normalization that never destroys the raw value: a value is returned as the pair `{ raw, canonical }`, where `raw` is the input byte for byte and `canonical` is the comparable form — the specification's §3.1 invariant that raw data stays recoverable, made structural rather than promised, and the evidence FR-109's `DPS-KI-NORMALIZE` catalog row already asks for. Six categories are normalized: Unicode and whitespace (NFC, plus the invisible spaces `s` does not match, plus the one Thai fold NFC misses — `สำ` written as NIKHAHIT + SARA AA renders identically to SARA AM and NFC leaves the two unequal), dates (Thai and Gregorian digits, four-digit Buddhist years without a hint, two-digit years only with a declared era), Thai telephone numbers to E.164, email with the domain lowercased and the local part left alone because RFC 5321 makes it case-sensitive, and organisation names by the lexical rule this requirement now owns. Stage 8 imports that rule rather than keeping a second copy, and the order is fixed and stated: normalization runs before extraction, so one mention is stripped once by one rule. Where the value does not decide, nothing is decided for it (SDD-061). Stage 4 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.

nodes.label: Document parsing into a structured artifact that keeps its link to the raw source: a document becomes a `ParsedArtifact` carrying `document_id`, `parsed_from`, `structure`, `text_blocks`, `tables`, `metadata` and `warnings` (spec §7 plus the warnings channel the refusals below report through), where `parsed_from` is the link back to the raw artifact FR-081 stored and `metadata` records the extractor version, so a reparse after a parser change is distinguishable from the original. This closes a gap that made the stages above it unreachable: `chunkDocument` (FR-112) consumes `blocks` and, before this, nothing in `src/` produced that shape — every caller was a test, so Stages 7 and 8 were two modules with no upstream. Parsing is deterministic and refuses structure that is not there: a `#` inside a fenced or indented code block is not a heading, `#hashtag` without a space is prose, a run of dashes with no text above it is a thematic break rather than a setext heading, a sentence containing a pipe is not a table, and a table whose separator disagrees with its header is reported and left as prose rather than read with a column dropped or invented. Markdown and plain text only; the formats needing a model or a binary keep arriving through FR-071's intake contract. Stage 2 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.

nodes.label: Derived-object provenance and the lineage chain back to a source: a knowledge object carries the ten fields §8 requires of anything that came from a source — `source_id`, `source_type`, `source_uri`, `source_version`, `artifact_id`, `ingested_at`, `parsed_at`, `pipeline_version`, `extractor_version`, `checksum` — and a derived object additionally names its `derivation_method` and the `source_objects` it came from, so the chain Fact → Chunk → ParsedArtifact → RawArtifact → Source can be walked and either reaches a source or says plainly that it did not. **This carries and validates a chain of identifiers it does not mint**: identity is established by FR-071's execution ledger and by Stage 2, and FR-116 consumes it — the moment it generated a `doc_id` it would have crossed into FR-071's subject rather than sitting beside it. The contract arrives after the field did: FR-112 and FR-113 have been passing a `provenance` object between them that nothing defined and nothing checked, and Stage 2 (FR-115) hands them one, and this is what gives that blob a meaning. Nothing is defaulted, an empty provenance is refused as loudly as an absent one, and an artifact parsed before it was ingested is refused because that order cannot have happened. Stage 3 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.

nodes.label: Deduplication and version relationships within one tenant: an artifact is placed against the ones already held as a `DUPLICATE_OF`, a `REVISION_OF`, or independent of all of them, using BR-021's four-part ingestion identity — source identity, source version, content hash and pipeline version — computed inside a tenant and never across one (SEC-021). Both rules have carried no code anchor since they were declared; this is what gives them one. A revision emits its supersession as a PAIR, `SUPERSEDES` from the incoming artifact and `SUPERSEDED_BY` back to the one it replaced, because a graph carrying only the forward edge cannot answer "what replaced this?" from the side that was replaced, which is the side that gets asked. A duplicate emits no edge, having replaced nothing. A reparse under a changed pipeline version is a revision rather than a duplicate even when every byte matches, which is what makes reprocessing a whole corpus safe after a parser change. Nothing is defaulted: a missing component of the key is refused rather than hashed as an empty string, because a hole in a key is not an absence but a value every other artifact missing that part will collide with. `DERIVED_FROM` is never assigned here — that edge is provenance and FR-116 owns it. Stage 6 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.

nodes.label: Per-stage failure attribution and BR-022 quarantine: a document that fails partway through the seven Tier 1 stages is quarantined with the complete failure envelope — `job_id`, `artifact_id`, `stage`, `error_code`, `error_message`, `retry_count`, `first_failed_at`, `last_failed_at`, `pipeline_version` — and classified retryable / non-retryable / review-required, rather than reported as nothing having happened. `runKnowledgeIngestionStagesWithTrace` extends FR-118's composition to catch each stage individually and report which succeeded before the one that did not, sharing every field mapping with the original throwing function (SDD-072) so neither duplicates the other. Every Tier 1 stage failure classifies `NON_RETRYABLE`: the seven stage functions are pure and deterministic, so a thrown validation error repeats identically on retry, and `REVIEW_REQUIRED` has no trigger either — an ambiguous value already declines via `canonical: null` (FR-114, SDD-061) rather than throwing, so it never reaches quarantine. `RETRYABLE`/`REVIEW_REQUIRED` stay in the vocabulary for failure modes this repository does not yet have (a network call, Tier 3/4 reporting) rather than being deleted for lack of a current trigger.

nodes.label: Import authorization is decided **once, on the resolved target Workspace**, in the pipeline that resolves it — not in each of the three route handlers, which is how three copies of a predicate drift. `authorizeImportTarget(viewer, workspace)` is the single entry point, it calls `ownsBusiness` rather than re-deriving ownership, and it is a required argument: a caller that omits the viewer throws at the call, in the manner `classify()` now requires its `scope`, so a fourth intake surface cannot be wired up unauthorized by simply not passing it. A Workspace above Business is refused rather than governed. The refusal is **evidence-backed, not conservatism**, and its justification is deliberately stated in two tenses because the first one expires. **Until FR-067 ships:** `Membership` is created in exactly two code paths and both set `businessId`, and the viewer contract exposes only Business-keyed grants (`visibleBusinessIds`, `ownedBusinessIds`, `domainsByBusinessId`) — so no principal can hold portfolio or tenant authority at all, and any rule written for it would be untestable, satisfiable by nothing and deniable of nothing. **Once FR-067 ships that premise is false and the refusal survives on a different, stronger reason:** a `WorkspaceMembership` is *collaboration* scope on the top-level container (keyed by `portfolioId`), and FR-067 AC-067.5 makes Tenant/Business/**Space**/Project assignment a separate audited mutation requiring the relevant owner authority — so holding it confers no write authority over a Space belonging to that Portfolio. AC-067.4 says the same thing from the read side: membership alone returns no hidden Project data, and import *creates* Project data. Two further facts make this more than a technicality — a portfolio-scoped Space carries **no `tenantId`** (`prisma/seed.js` WS-PLATFORM sets only `portfolioId`), so it sits above the BR-001 isolation boundary, and one Portfolio spans every Tenant beneath it. Opening a write path there on portfolio-level membership would put a write above the boundary the whole scope chain rests on. What would legitimately unlock it is neither FR-067 nor a looser predicate: it is a Space-level owner authority carried in the viewer contract — the FR-061 shape again — after which `AUTHORIZERS` gains an entry, never before. Inventing a rule at the end of a security fix is how the fix becomes the next incident. The three routes leave `docs/.route-viewer-baseline.json` when this lands; the baseline shrinks, it is never edited to accommodate them.

A clean dry run commits; a failed one reverts the optimistic edge and prints the reason at the edge rather than in a toast that outlives its context. Undo rides the audit event. A future surface that cannot honour this adds a converter, never a second write path. FR-083, FR-084; BR-009, BR-017, SDD-008, SDD-009, ADR-035

nodes.label: Projects Overview is one composed read model behind one route (`GET /api/projects/overview`): the KPI counts and the list rows, progress included, in a single response. A progress bar per row would otherwise mean one `/api/progress/project/{id}` call per project — an N+1 across the page's main content. It follows SDD-045's discipline: authorize the scope before composing, read through the pure calculators, never mutate `progressCache` on a read, and leave the existing `/api/projects` list contract untouched so its consumers do not move (the cost of moving it is recorded in `.brain/rca/2026-08-18-project-list-envelope-broke-relation-consumers.md`).

nodes.label: Observability is one emitter and one correlation id, not logging scattered through the call path. `src/lib/observability` exposes a structured emitter whose sink is injectable (stdout by default, captured in tests) and whose field names are **allowlisted**: safety comes from what the emitter accepts, not from scrubbing what a caller passed, because a denylist only ever knows the secrets someone already thought of. An unknown field is omitted and its *name* listed in `unsafeFieldsOmitted`, so a dropped field is visible rather than silent. The correlation id is validated before use (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$`) since it arrives as untrusted input and is echoed into records. It flows route → turn → ingest → `AuditEvent.payloadJson`, which makes the audit table — not the log stream — the durable join between a webhook delivery and the rows it created. Counts and durations ride on the batch record; a metrics backend is deliberately not introduced.

nodes.label: The conversation reader is one composed read model (`src/modules/crm/conversation-read-model.js`) behind two routes, and it holds no write path at all. Its query count is **constant in the number of conversations**: the last message per conversation and the per-conversation message count each come from one grouped query over the page's conversation ids, never one query per row — the same N+1 discipline SDD-047 imposes on the Projects Dashboard, and the reason a read model exists here rather than a `include: { messages: true }` on the list. Authorization runs *before* composition: the viewer's Tenant is resolved from the selected Business, and a conversation owned by a Business outside `visibleBusinessIds` is excluded by the query, not filtered out of a result that was already fetched (SEC-001). `channel` and `direction` render from `enums.js` rather than from hand-copied literals. Message bodies are customer PII and reach the browser only inside this authorized response; they are never logged, and the observability emitter's allowlist (SDD-048) already refuses them.

nodes.label: Recording a reply is a **separate, narrow writer** in the crm module (`reply-record-service`), not a `direction: 'OUTBOUND'` call into `ingestLineMessage`. The ingest seam creates a Person, a Customer and a Conversation when they are absent, and that is exactly wrong here: a receipt naming a conversation that does not exist is an error to report, never a reason to invent one. So the writer resolves the inbound `Message` first, derives the conversation from it, and refuses anything it cannot place — the conversation is never taken from the request, which is what makes cross-tenant attachment impossible rather than merely checked. It appends one row and one `AuditEvent` in a single transaction, exactly as the ingest seam does, and carries the same correlation id (SDD-048) so `webhook → turn → message → reply` remains one chain in the audit table. The route is a batch like the webhook: a per-receipt failure is captured with the stage that failed and never drops the rest, because a transport that has already sent three replies must be able to report all three.

nodes.label: The seventeen-stage knowledge ingestion pipeline reuses the FR-071 execution ledger rather than declaring new models. At the storage layer that is free: `dataPipelineDefinitionId` and `pipelineStageId` are plain `String` columns with no enum, no relation and no check constraint (`prisma/schema.prisma`), so a new definition id and seventeen new `DPS-*` stage ids need no migration. At the contract layer it is not free, and saying so is the point of this decision: `zPipelineEvent` and `zPipelineRunInput` pin `dataPipelineDefinitionId` and `executionContractId` with `z.literal`, `pipelineStageId` is refined against the ten-entry FR-071 catalog (`src/platform/integrations/core/pipeline-tracking-contract.js`), and the tracking service materializes that one catalog on every run creation — so `DPL-KNOWLEDGE-INGEST-V1` is rejected today, and the first implementation slice must parameterize the FR-071 envelope by definition id before it can register anything. That is a change to implemented, tested FR-071 code, named here rather than discovered later. A second execution ledger remains the wrong answer: it would give one question two answers and make the reconciliation evidence something that has to be believed twice. `PipelineRecordEvent` already carries `docId` / `picId` / `factId` — written on every record event and read by provenance-filtered replay, with no producer supplying a non-null value today — and knowledge ingestion reuses their existing FR-071 meaning rather than redefining it.

nodes.label: Knowledge ingestion stage execution location is policy-driven, not deployment-driven. The specification's split (Stages 1–8 local edge, 9–14 cloud GKS, 15–17 selected execution) is an illustrative default, not the contract: the binding input is the data's own classification, so RESTRICTED knowledge carrying `cloud_processing_allowed = false` runs all seventeen stages locally and no topology or environment change may override that. Location is therefore resolved per object from FR-111's policy fields at each stage boundary, never read from deployment configuration — a data boundary that configuration can widen is not a boundary.

nodes.label: Chunking is a pure calculator in the knowledge lane, with no persistence and no model. `src/modules/knowledge/chunking.js` takes parsed blocks plus a scope and a provenance and returns chunk objects; it opens no database, writes no table and declares no Prisma model, so the knowledge charter's `owns_models: []` stays true (SDD-057, ADR-050). Persisting chunks is a later slice and will need a charter change — pinning the boundary here makes it a decision rather than an oversight. Token counting is a whitespace approximation on purpose: a model tokenizer would couple Stage 7 to whichever embedding model Stage 15 happens to use, and this number exists to choose a split point, not to be billed against. Exactness belongs at the embedding boundary, where the model is known.

nodes.label: Entity recognition is a seam with a deterministic default, not a model dependency. `extractEntityCandidates` takes an optional `recognizer`; the default recognises legal-form organisation patterns only — `บริษัท … จำกัด`, `ห้างหุ้นส่วนจำกัด …`, `… Co., Ltd.` — because in those the suffix IS the evidence: the grammar announces the type without anyone recognising the name inside it. Person, product, location and the rest of §13's type list need a model, and a model in the knowledge lane would couple Stage 8 to whatever recognises Thai and English text this month (the SDD-059 reasoning, one stage over). An empty seam was rejected as the alternative: shipping a hook with nothing behind it is what makes Stage 15 embedding read as delivered when it is not, and this requirement declines to repeat that shape. `normalized_name` is lexical and uses only the mention itself — trim, collapse, strip the legal wrapper. The moment it consults a registry, a catalogue or the other candidates in the batch it has begun deciding two mentions are one thing, and that decision is Stage 9's.

nodes.label: A normalizer that cannot decide reports the ambiguity instead of resolving it — and reports it by withholding the canonical value, not by attaching a warning beside one. A warning next to a readable field is a warning somebody skips: if `canonical` holds a guess, a caller will use it. So an undecidable value returns `canonical: null` with the reason, and the caller has nothing else to read. The case that sets the rule is a Thai date like `25/8/26`, which is 2526 BE or 2026 CE with nothing in the string to separate them — forty-three years apart, both plausible, and no downstream check can catch the wrong one. The same withholding covers an undeclared field order (`5/8/69`, where day and month are both twelve or under) and a date that does not exist (`31/2/2569`, which must never roll into March). Six of §9's twelve categories are normalized; currency, unit, product code, country/region, timezone and identifier format are declined for a stronger reason than missing locale data — their canonical form is business-configured, so one invented here would be wrong in a way that looks authoritative.

nodes.label: Widening what knowledge may carry must not widen what knowledge is served. `business-contract.js` holds two decisions that share a word: the record schema, which says what may be STORED, and the query filter, which says what is SERVED to a public surface. FR-111 widens the first to the four-level lattice and leaves the second at `PUBLIC`, and the two are separate on purpose rather than by oversight. The failure this pins against is not somebody deliberately opening the filter — it is somebody reading `record.sensitivity === 'PUBLIC'`, seeing that the enum now has four values, and correcting the comparison because it looks stale. It is not stale; it is the boundary. The packet stops asserting its own label and verifies it instead: it refuses to wrap a record above `PUBLIC` rather than stamping `PUBLIC` on whatever it was handed, so a future widening of the filter fails loudly instead of leaking. The lattice lives in `src/lib/validation/enums.js` and is named `KNOWLEDGE_SENSITIVITY_LEVELS` because `sensitivity` already means FR-026 action sensitivity (LOW/HIGH) elsewhere; `write-tools.js` rejects an action sensitivity outside LOW/HIGH so a knowledge value cannot reach that path, but `agent/auth-context.js` validates nothing and already defaults to the string `PUBLIC` — so the separation rests on naming there rather than on a guard, and saying so is the point of pinning it.

nodes.label: The parser produces the block shape Stage 7 already consumes. `parseDocument` returns `structure` as an array of `{ type: heading or text, level, text }`, which is exactly the `blocks` argument `chunkDocument` reads — so Stage 2 hands Stage 7 its input rather than the two agreeing by coincidence across two test suites that each build the shape. **Stage 7 owns the shape**; it existed first and its tests define it, and the parser conforms to it. The seam is held by a test that feeds real parser output straight into `chunkDocument` and asserts on the resulting chunks, because a written statement that two shapes match is prose, and prose is not a contract — the same reason a green governance run does not prove a link resolves. Markdown and plain text are parsed here; PDF, DOCX, OCR and vision layout are not, and are received instead through FR-071's `smartgift.document-intake.v1` front door, which validates someone else's extraction rather than performing one.

nodes.label: Declaring knowledge derived is a claim that names its sources, not an exemption from having any. Spec §8 forbids publishing a Fact or Relation whose source cannot be traced "unless explicitly declared DERIVED / INFERRED / COMPUTED", which read naively is an escape hatch: type the word and the requirement lifts. The declaration therefore exempts an object from having a RAW source and never from having sources — an object that declares itself derived and can name nothing is not derived, it is unattributed, and it does not publish. Naming is not enough either: `assertPublishable` requires a resolver and refuses a named source that nothing resolves, because a check that accepts an unresolvable name lets the declaration back itself, which is the laundering this decision exists to stop arriving through the door the decision built. There is deliberately no shape-only mode; whether a named source exists is the question, and a permissive default would answer a different one.

nodes.label: Cross-tenant deduplication is made inexpressible rather than forbidden. Content similarity and structural similarity are declined, and not merely as unimplemented: both require a threshold, and a threshold chosen in this module would be a judgement about which documents count as "the same" made by whoever typed the number and inherited by everyone after. The same reasoning declines inferring a lineage from a filename — `contract-v1.pdf` beside `contract-v2.pdf` is a hint a human left, not a claim the system can verify.

nodes.label: A knowledge ingestion run input is derived whole from the artifact's ingestion identity, its correlation id included, because FR-071 compares more than the key. `createPipelineRun` returns `UNCHANGED` for a repeated `idempotencyKey` only when `requestHash` also matches, and that hash covers the entire parsed input — so a second ingestion of the same artifact carrying a fresh correlation id raises 409 `idempotency key was reused with different input` rather than being the no-op BR-021 requires. `knowledgeIngestionRunInput` therefore computes every field from the artifact, and re-ingestion is byte-identical by construction rather than by the caller remembering to make it so. nodes.row_text: The execution monitor has read `PipelineRun.actualCount` / `.failedCount` since before anything wrote them — `@default(0)`, and `mode-bodies.jsx` renders `Failed` in the normal ink specifically because it is zero. That is not an empty panel; it is a false one, indistinguishable on screen from a real zero. `recordPipelineEvent` now aggregates the run's counts from every `PipelineStep` row sharing its `runId` whenever an event supplies a count — real summed integers, not nulls, so the same `  0` coercion in `runSummary`/`stepSummary` that would have silently absorbed a null has nothing to undermine. Aggregate-on-completion, not finalization-only: a run half done showing a final-looking zero would be the same defect in slower motion, and knowledge-ingestion runs never reach `RUN_FINISHED` in this repository (ADR-050 D3) — finalization-only would mean never. The aggregate sums every step row sharing a `runId`, which assumes one row per stage per run; `(runId, pipelineStageId)` carries no uniqueness constraint, only a non-unique index, so a stage retried under a fresh `executionStepId` would be double-counted rather than reporting its true count. Nothing today constructs that — SDD-069 materializes each stage's step once and reuses it; replay creates its steps under a new `runId`, never summed into the original. A second row is not a hypothetical the design left open: the step state machine retries a stage in place — `REPLAYING: ['REPLAYING', 'RUNNING', 'SUCCEEDED', 'FAILED']`, on the same row — and ADR-030's own rejected-alternatives table names the other direction, reusing ids across a retry, as overwriting history and making the result non-auditable. So `(runId, pipelineStageId)` staying unenforced is a real gap against the design's own intent, not an open question — `@@unique([runId, pipelineStageId])` is very likely correct, pending a check for existing duplicate rows before any migration can apply it. Pinned by two tests, not fixed ahead of that check: a fake-db unit test recording today's behaviour against a fake that cannot enforce a uniqueness constraint and would silently go stale the moment a migration lands, and a real-database integration test constructing the same duplicate directly — the one that will actually start failing, at the `create` call rather than at an assertion, the day the constraint exists. NFR-020; SDD-070, SDD-069, ADR-030

nodes.label: FR-118's seven stage-invocation steps are extracted into one shared definition (`TIER1_STEPS`) that both `runKnowledgeIngestionStages` and a new `runKnowledgeIngestionStagesWithTrace` iterate, so the field mappings — checksum from content_hash, a chunk's scope as the identity pair alone, and the rest SDD-068 already named — are written once rather than duplicated between a throwing caller and a trace-collecting one. `runKnowledgeIngestionStages` keeps its exact throw-on-first-failure contract; all fifteen of its existing tests pass unchanged, because its observable behaviour did not change, only its internals. The new function never throws itself: a stage's exception becomes data (`{success, stages, envelope, partialEnvelope, failedStage, error}`), because the reason to call it instead of the throwing version is to keep going long enough to report where it stopped. `errorRef` stays redacted on the FR-071 ledger, per that contract's own repeated description of `PipelineRecordEvent`/`PipelineStep` as carrying "redacted" evidence, most concretely AC-071.28 ("agents emit only append-only, redacted events"). This was a **caller-side convention with no contract enforcement** at the moment this slice was written — `errorRef: z.string().max(1000)` accepted anything. A peer session found the same gap independently while reviewing this slice and closed it separately: `errorRef` is now a validated reference token (SDD-073, `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/#@-]*$/`, max 200). Both `errorRef` values this slice writes — `ki-quarantine://{identity}/{stage}` and `ki-quarantine://{identity}/record` — were checked against that pattern directly before this row was written and conform with room to spare. `error_message` (BR-022's field) therefore lives only in the quarantine envelope this executor returns to its own caller; the ledger's `errorRef` holds a stable reference (`ki-quarantine://{identity}/{stage}`) instead. `retryable`, a boolean, cannot carry BR-022's three-way classification — only `RETRYABLE` maps to `true`; `REVIEW_REQUIRED` maps to `false` alongside `NON_RETRYABLE`, since "a human must act" and "retrying alone will not" are both true of it, and the full classification travels in the envelope regardless of what the shared boolean can hold. `retry_count` is always `0` and `first_failed_at`/`last_failed_at` always coincide — no retry-within-run mechanism exists (the same gap SDD-071 names for NFR-020's identical field), so there is exactly one attempt to time.

nodes.label: `errorRef` on the pipeline event envelope is a reference to an error, never the error itself, and the contract now enforces the shape rather than trusting the caller. FR-071 states the redaction rule four times — `PipelineStep`/`PipelineRecordEvent` as "one redacted record outcome per attempt", the "redacted append-only evidence outbox", keeping "restricted document payloads separate from redacted pipeline events", and AC-071.28's "emit only append-only, redacted" events — and enforced it nowhere: the field was `z.string().trim().min(1).max(1000)`, which accepts a stack trace, an exception message or a quoted document fragment, on a ledger that is append-only and therefore cannot take a payload back. The rule lived entirely in caller discipline at a moment when BR-022 was about to make the field carry real failure text for the first time. `errorRef` is now a reference token — ASCII alphanumerics plus the separators a handle uses, capped at 200 — which every value in the repository already satisfied (`err://event-1`). The rule is an ALLOWED ALPHABET rather than a rejected separator on purpose: rejecting whitespace reads as sufficient in English and is not, because Thai does not separate words with spaces, so a whole Thai sentence is one whitespace-free token and would have passed a space/newline check untouched — in a product whose user-facing copy is Thai, that is the likelier shape of a real error message, not the exotic one. Stated as a bound rather than a guarantee: this blocks the accident — passing `err.message` or `err.stack` straight through — and not a determined caller, who can still join a sentence with underscores; a conforming value is not evidence that the reference carries nothing sensitive. The full human-readable message belongs in the caller's own return value, never on the shared ledger.
